title: cbatch-regression-scratchpad
content:
Personal scratchpad / breadcrumbs for the throughput regression observed after the recent cbatch config change. Informal notes, commands I ran, error snippets, and quick hypotheses.

Timeline / quick summary:
- 2026-03-10 ~13:50 PDT: deploy of cbatch tuning flags (auto-rollout: cbatch-max-batch-tokens=1536, cbatch-latency-ms=12).
- 2026-03-10 ~14:00: saw production P95 latency stable but aggregate tokens/sec dropped ~40% for multi-client gen workloads.
- Baseline before deploy: ~270-300k tokens/s on 4xA100 cluster (mixed short+long sequences). After: ~120-170k tokens/s depending on workload.

Repro steps I used locally / infra: (commands I ran)
- Run simple load test (same client load as prod-sim):
  python tools/loadgen.py --target http://host:8080/generate --concurrency 64 --seq_len 1024 --payloads tests/payloads/multi-seq.json 

- Kubernetes logs:
  kubectl -n inference logs deploy/serving-runtime --since=1h | egrep "cbatch|batch|kv-cache" -A3 -B2
  # grep showed many "batch_count=1, tokens_in_batch=2048" entries after deploy

- Sample pod-level profiling:
  nsys profile --output=nsys_cbatch_run3 --trace=cuda,osrt -f true -- python tools/run_single_client.py --seq 1024 --requests 200
  # exported timeline, saw many small inference kernels with low utilization

Observed snippets / errors (copied raw):
- [2026-03-10T14:03:22Z] ERROR serving-runtime cbatch: AssertionError: tokens_in_batch (2048) > continuous_batching.max_batch_tokens (1536)
- [2026-03-10T14:04:05Z] WARN kv_cache: key_cache_miss_rate=0.47, cache_warmup_epoch=3
- worker-12 stderr: RuntimeWarning: padding ratio high (0.68) -> inefficient packing

Immediate notes on these log lines:
- The assertion message implies the runtime is still producing batches with token count > configured limit. Two possibilities: 1) internal accounting uses tokens_per_sequence != what config expects (off-by-one due to EOS/forced tokens), or 2) there are race conditions where per-request token length increases during packing (dynamic length adjustments).
- High padding ratio + cache_miss suggests request shape variance (long tail sequences) leading to lots of small/inefficient batches. That explains lower GPU kernel occupancy and much lower tokens/sec.

Config excerpts I checked (production cluster):
- /etc/serving/config.yaml (relevant bits):
  continuous_batching:
    enabled: true
    max_batch_tokens: 1536
    max_concurrent_batches: 48
    latency_ms: 12
    padding_strategy: right

- Runtime report (from /var/log/engine/runtime_report.log):
  runtime.cbatch: reported_config.max_batch_tokens=4096  # WTF - mismatch between config file and effective config

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Config drift between control-plane and agent (agent thinks max_batch_tokens=4096 while control-plane rollback set 1536) -> leads to inconsistent kernel selection and potential assertion when other checks enforced.
2) padding_strategy=right vs left: right-padding with variable-length streams reduces coalescing opportunities for continuous batching (we generally do better with left pad for streaming request shapes).
3) KV cache warmup: when cache miss rate is high, sequence lengths effectively vary a lot (first tokens include prefix + full context), so batching efficiency drops.
4) A recent change in packer code introduced an off-by-one for the EOS token causing token accounting mismatch.
5) Host CPU throttling (observed high CPU steal on node) triggered slower packing loop -> fewer batches pushed to GPU, lower throughput.

Quick experiments to run (in order):
- A: Force a single known-good config on agent (set runtime env SERVING_CBATCH_MAX=1536 via k8s env and restart) and rerun load test. Compare tokens/sec.
- B: Disable continuous_batching (continuous_batching.enabled=false) and compare latency/throughput. If throughputs jump back to baseline, direct pointer to cbatch implementation/regression.
- C: Toggle padding_strategy to left and run load test against a synthetic mix of seq lengths (short, med, long).
- D: Instrument packer to emit histogram of tokens_in_batch (write to /tmp/batch_hist.tsv) and collect for 30m under load.
- E: Capture nsys for a run with cbatch on vs off to inspect kernel fusion/stream utilization.

Commands to run for A and B (copyable):
- kubectl set env deploy/serving-runtime SERVING_CBATCH_MAX=1536 -n inference && kubectl rollout restart deploy/serving-runtime -n inference
- kubectl patch deploy/serving-runtime -n inference --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/0/value","value":"false"}]' # (for disabling - adapt index)

Profiling checklist (what to capture):
- nsys timeline (GPU kernels + OS) for 60s at steady state
- runtime internal traces: enable DEBUG_Cbatch=1 and collect /var/log/engine/pack_trace.log
- collect /proc/stat and iostat for nodes to rule out host throttles

Notes about reproducibility:
- The regression appears stronger with mixed-length workloads (our PLG demo traffic type). Pure short-seq workloads show <15% change. So prefilter traffic to reproduce reliably.
- Load generator: include a realistic prefix distribution (50% short <64, 40% med 256-512, 10% long 1024+). I saved a sample JSON at gs://redwood-loadtests/cbatch/sample_mix.json.

Open TODOs / next steps for me:
- [ ] Run experiment A (force agent config) and document tokens/sec before/after (timeline: today EOD).
- [ ] Add histogram logging in packer and ship a tiny patch to dev branch for quick deploy. (PR draft: /pull/930 - TODO add tests).
- [ ] Ask infra to check node CPU steal/steal_time during the window 13:45-14:15 on 2026-03-10 (ticket INF-4721 assigned).
- [ ] If A fails, try B (disable cbatch) to see delta.
- [ ] If B restores throughput, prepare hotfix: revert cbatch change + add stronger assertions + telemetry for tokens_in_batch distribution.

Random notes / observations while poking:
- I noticed runtime_report.log had inconsistent reported_config entries across pods. Might indicate that config templating / rollout hasn't propagated to some agents (race during rollout).
- One pod had a much older binary (v1.14.2) while others were on v1.15.0. Need to verify image tag pinning in the helm chart.

Useful links (for later):
- Load test results bucket: gs://redwood-loadtests/cbatch/2026-03-10-run3
- Infra ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4721
- Candidate PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/930 (WIP: packer histogram)

Notes to future-me: keep this doc around until we close INF-4721 and roll a stable fix. Remove any hardcoded secrets before sharing.

-end of scratchpad-
